journeys.claim: A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a Claude PTY session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host independently records the prompt and decision.

A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a headless Claude session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host records the prompt once and the provider receives exactly one allow.

A person sends one prompt through the real terminal client to a Codex session, sees that exact prompt reflected once, answers one permission request once, and sees the turn finish; the host records the prompt once and the provider receives exactly one allow.

A real first run on one host makes its replica of another host's agent; with the origin out of reach a fresh client paints the cached chat from its own store with the host away and the composer waiting, keeps a draft, appends the origin's new turn once when the link returns, keeps its rows on screen through a Reset until the rebuilt transcript swaps in, and reconnects by itself when its own daemon restarts, sending the kept draft.

A laptop that has never paired finds a desk on its network: the hosts overlay lists it as found, not paired, with the command that pairs it, and `amux peers` names it by the desk's own host id. Six digits the desk printed, typed once into `amux pair desk`, pair the two and name the desk by that id, and the desk lists the laptop as paired. The client that was running all along shows the desk online and direct, opens the desk's agent, and sends one prompt the desk records once and answers; the person leaves and the client exits cleanly.

Two machines signed in to one account reach each other only through the relay. A second profile on the laptop opens on its own empty fleet. On the default profile the desk's agent answers a prompt; the laptop then signs out, the desk goes away on screen, and a message written then is held on the laptop and never reaches the desk. Signed in again, the chat is current and the held message reaches the desk once.

From the fleet a person creates a Claude agent on the desk and it answers; renames it and the desk lists the same agent under the new name; stops it and the desk lists it exited with its prompt and reply kept; resumes it from the exited composer with a message and the desk lists the same agent live again, each prompt held once; and deletes it, after which neither the fleet nor the desk has it.

On the laptop a person writes to an agent on the desk: text, a twelve-line paste that stands in the sentence as one token, more text, and a review of the diff the desk computed of the agent's working tree, with a comment on one changed line. The desk receives one prompt holding those four in that order, the paste's exact text and the comment on that line, and the review names a patch whose bytes on the desk's disk hash to that name and hold the edit. Opening the chat again shows the tokens as they were sent.

A phone nobody has signed in on offers Sign In on the You tab; the hand-off names the account service it sends the person to and comes back signed in, and the account service is asked to sign in and to hand over the account's session. That session's relay, and only it, carries the pairing to a machine that shares no network with the phone: the machine is listed under its own name, its agent opens, and the machine receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it.

Signed in to an account that has bought nothing, the relay lists the account's machine and carries nothing to it, so a pairing link through the relay is refused. Bought at the App Store while amux.sh cannot be reached, the purchase is kept and the paywall says it is not confirmed; with amux.sh answering again, Restore Purchases offers the App Store's subscription to amux.sh, which takes it, and the paywall says the account is subscribed. The relay link then reads what the account buys, carries the pairing, and the machine receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it.

On a phone signed in and paired through the relay, the system's screenshot makes the app offer Report over the frame it froze; the report opens on that frame and takes a note. amux.sh refuses it in its own words and nothing written is lost; Retry hands over the same report and comes back with a receipt. The report that left the phone, read where it crossed into the account service, carries the note and the frozen screen, and the machine lists the agent that screen showed.

The app, saying it draws at an accessibility text size, pairs with a machine on the keypad, opens a Claude agent and sends it a prompt; the permission card it raises is read and answered with Allow once at that size, the machine holds the prompt once and finishes the turn, and the provider receives exactly one allow.

With the local network refused, the Hosts tab says so, offers the setting that undoes it and lists no machine; granted, the phone's own browser finds the machine on its network and offers it. The amux://pair link the machine printed, opened from outside the app as the system hands a scanned code over, names the machine before anything is trusted; trusted, the machine is listed under its own name and receives the prompt written on the phone exactly once and answers it.

A phone paired with a machine running two agents is put away. At the machine one agent comes to need the person and the other answers a question. A push built from journeys/fixtures/needs-you.apns names the first: xcrun simctl push shows its notification, and because this simulator never hands a push's payload to an app put away, the debug door hands the same payload to the app's remote-notification handler with the app held in the background, as iOS calls it for a push that wakes the app; the handler brings that one chat current and nothing else: with the machine stopped and the app brought back to the foreground, the named agent's chat holds its ask and the other agent's chat does not hold the answer it gave while the app was away. In the foreground, with the machine running again, the other agent catches up without being named, and the ask answered on the phone reaches the machine, which finishes the turn.

Three agents, one of each kind, are mid-turn when amux is killed; they finish their turns into their journals with no daemon, outlive their grace and exit. Any amux command starts amux again under its supervisor, which finds them exited; a newer build is installed under the supervisor and activated; every finished turn is in the store, and resuming the exited agents loses nothing.

retired_phone_journeys.about: Phone journeys written for the app before it ran on one runtime per profile. Each claim is carried by the stories named beside it.

journeys.how: Found by the phone's own browser and paired by the printed code with the machine's name and key before trust, with no account (reach-host); the machine away and reached again with nobody pressing anything (leave-and-recover); the local network refused, said so and where it is undone (local-network).
The fleet and a chat drawn from the phone's own store before any host answers (leave-and-recover's fresh client with the origin away, push-wake's fleet with the machine stopped).

Remembered rows kept on screen with the host away and confirmed when it answers (leave-and-recover); every listed agent current again in the foreground (push-wake); a row opened to its chat and the back chevron returning to the fleet (reach-host).

A chat read and a prompt the host receives exactly once, per kind (conversation-decision stories); the host away said where the composer goes and a message held until it can be sent (leave-and-recover); the changes the host computed opened from the chat (attachment-or-review).

A permission answered on the phone and the host and provider receiving exactly what was pressed, per kind (conversation-decision stories), at an accessibility size (accessibility) and after a push woke the app (push-wake). The other ask bodies are held by the chat's component snapshots.
A patch the host computed read on the phone, a line selected and remarked on, and the review sent with the message; the host holds one prompt carrying the review.

A long paste standing in the sentence as one token and a review attached, one message the host receives once (attachment-or-review); an agent renamed, stopped and resumed from the chat's menu (manage-agent); a message written while the host is away held and delivered once (leave-and-recover).

New Agent creates Claude on the machine and it answers (manage-agent); headless and terminal Claude sessions each open under their own identity and round-trip a prompt the host observes (conversation-decision stories).

A machine restarted underneath recovered with nobody pressing anything (leave-and-recover); put away, nothing is kept current but a pushed chat, and brought back every agent is listed again (push-wake).

The printed code reaching the machine's name and key before trust (reach-host); a pairing link handed over from outside the app (local-network); an agent started on the machine (manage-agent); a second account on its own profile that knows none of the first account's machines (keep-authority); a restart recovered from (leave-and-recover).

The hand-off to the account service and back signed in (account-sign-in); a purchase kept when amux.sh cannot confirm it and restored to the account (purchase-restore); a second account added on its own profile, signed out and back in (keep-authority).
A screenshot's offer over the frozen frame, a note, a refusal in the account service's words, Retry sending the same report for a receipt, and the report read where it left the phone.
A machine paired, a chat read and a permission answered with the app drawn at an accessibility text size it states itself; VoiceOver names and hit sizes are held by the accessibility audit.
Signing in through the scripted account service starts the runtime at the relay the handed-over session names; after pairing, Hosts shows the machine and its agent answers.
An account with nothing bought is refused a machine only the relay reaches; once amux.sh says it is subscribed, the link reads that again and the machine is reached through the relay.
Paired and reading a machine with no account anywhere (reach-host), and the machine going away and coming back with nobody pressing anything (leave-and-recover).
A second account on the phone is a profile of its own, with no machines and an empty fleet, beside the first; signing out keeps the account listed.
